items.bodyEn: Coming down from the Suzuka Pass, travelers reached Tsuchiyama, the first post town in Ōmi Province, with two honjin and around forty inns. Hiroshige's print Tsuchiyama: Spring Rain shows a lord's procession crossing the Tamura River bridge in slanting rain toward the dark grove of Tamura Shrine, dedicated to the general Sakanoue no Tamuramaro (758–811).
items.sourceNote: Hiroshige, Hōeidō Tōkaidō (c. 1833), 'Tsuchiyama: Haru no ame'; 東海道宿村大概帳 (1843)

items.bodyEn: Packhorse drivers on the Suzuka Pass sang: the slope is sunny, Suzuka is clouded, and Tsuchiyama in between gets rain. The Suzuka magouta, their traditional song, maps the weather of a single day's walk from Sakashita over the pass. Hiroshige painted Tsuchiyama in exactly that rain, and the line is still quoted whenever the town is named.
items.ja: {坂|さか}は{照|て}る{照|て}る{鈴鹿|すずか}は{曇|くも}る、あいの{土山|つちやま}{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}る
items.kana: さかはてるてるすずかはくもる、あいのつちやまあめがふる

items.titleEn: 几帳面: Precision From a Curtain Stand
items.bodyEn: 几帳面, meticulous, hides a piece of Heian furniture. A 几帳 was a portable curtain stand used to screen a noble's room. Its posts were finished with a special edge: the corner planed off and fine grooves cut along both sides. That precise profile was called 几帳面, and in time a person finished to that standard was 几帳面 as well.

items.titleEn: きらい That Is Not Dislike
items.bodyEn: In this station's 〜きらいがある, きらい is not 'dislike'. The noun 嫌い also means a tendency or trace, and that is the sense here: 独断に走るきらいがある, there is a tendency to act on one's own. It names unwelcome tendencies only, is almost always written in kana, and belongs to essays and reviews rather than chat.
items.ja: {独断|どくだん}に{走|はし}るきらいがある
items.kana: どくだんにはしるきらいがある
